commands.description: Adds two values. Numbers, complex numbers, lists and matrices all work.
Subtracts the second value from the first. Works on numbers, complex numbers, lists and matrices.
Multiplies two values. A list or matrix times a number scales each element.
Divides the first value by the second.

commands.name: SIN
commands.description: Sine of an angle, read in the angle mode set in MODES.

examples.comment: The angle mode is radians: π/6 is 30 degrees

commands.name: COS
commands.description: Cosine of an angle in the current angle mode.

commands.name: TAN
commands.description: Tangent of an angle in the current angle mode.

examples.comment: The angle mode is radians: π/4 is 45 degrees

commands.name: ASIN
commands.description: The angle whose sine is the value, from −90° to 90° (or the same range in radians or grads). Complex results are possible.

commands.name: ACOS
commands.description: The angle whose cosine is the value, from 0° to 180° (or the same range in radians or grads). Outside −1 to 1 the result is complex.

commands.name: ATAN
commands.description: The angle whose tangent is the value, from −90° to 90° (or the same range in radians or grads).

commands.name: LN
commands.description: Logarithm to base e. Complex arguments work.

commands.name: eˣ
commands.description: e to the power of the value. Complex arguments work.

commands.name: LOG
commands.description: Logarithm to base 10.

commands.name: 10ˣ
commands.description: 10 to the power of the value.

commands.name: x²
commands.description: Squares the value before it.
Square root of the value after it. Negative and complex values give complex roots.
Raises the value before it to the power after it.

commands.name: NTHROOT
commands.description: Root of a given degree: the degree goes before NTHROOT, the value after it.

examples.comment: The cube root of 8; the degree 3 comes first

commands.name: x⁻¹
commands.description: One divided by the value. For a square matrix, its inverse.

commands.name: ABS
commands.description: Size of a value without its sign. For a complex value (x,y), its distance from the origin.

commands.name: NEG
commands.description: Changes the sign of the value after it. Complex numbers work.

commands.name: EEX
commands.description: Starts the power-of-ten part of a number: 2E3 is 2000.

commands.name: Ans
commands.description: The result of the last calculation, for use in the next one.

examples.comment: Ans is the 42 from the line above, so the second line adds 1 to it

commands.name: STO▶
commands.description: Stores the value on its left in the variable named on its right.

commands.name: π
commands.description: The constant π, 3.14159265359.
Factorial of the value before it. For fractions it gives the gamma function of the value plus one.

commands.name: Σ
commands.description: Sum of an expression as a variable runs from a start value to an end value: Σ(variable=start,end,expression).

examples.comment: The squares of K for K from 1 to 5, added up

commands.name: ARG
commands.description: Angle from the positive real axis to a complex value (x,y), in the current angle mode.

examples.comment: The angle mode is radians: (1,1) lies at π/4, which is 45 degrees

commands.name: AND
commands.description: 1 when both values are non-zero, else 0.
Differentiates an expression: ∂ is followed by the variable and the expression in brackets. Use a formal name (s1 to s5) to get a symbolic result.

examples.comment: Differentiates s1^2+3*s1 with respect to s1; the name s1 keeps the result symbolic

commands.description: Integrates an expression between two limits: ∫(lower,upper,expression,variable). With a formal name (s1 to s5) as a limit the result is symbolic.

examples.comment: The area under 2*X from X = 0 to X = 1

commands.description: Builds an equation from two expressions. It is not a test and stores nothing.

commands.name: TAYLOR
commands.description: Taylor polynomial of an expression in a variable around 0, to the order given: TAYLOR(expression,variable,order).

commands.name: CONJ
commands.description: Flips the sign of the imaginary part: (3,4) becomes (3,−4).

commands.name: IM
commands.description: Imaginary part: y of the complex value (x,y).

commands.name: RE
commands.description: Real part: x of the complex value (x,y).

commands.name: e
commands.description: The base of natural logarithms, 2.71828182846.

commands.name: i
commands.description: The square root of −1, written (0,1).

commands.name: MAXREAL
commands.description: The largest real number the calculator holds, 9.99999999999E499.

commands.name: MINREAL
commands.description: The smallest positive real number the calculator holds, 1E−499.

commands.name: ACOSH
commands.description: Inverse of COSH.

commands.name: ASINH
commands.description: Inverse of SINH.

commands.name: ATANH
commands.description: Inverse of TANH.

commands.name: COSH
commands.description: Hyperbolic cosine. Complex arguments work.

commands.name: SINH
commands.description: Hyperbolic sine. Complex arguments work.

commands.name: TANH
commands.description: Hyperbolic tangent. Complex arguments work.

commands.name: ALOG
commands.description: 10 to the power of the value, computed more exactly than with ^.

commands.name: EXP
commands.description: e to the power of the value, computed more exactly than with ^.

commands.name: EXPM1
commands.description: e to the power of the value, minus 1. Keeps its precision for values close to zero.

commands.name: LNP1
commands.description: Natural logarithm of the value plus 1. Keeps its precision for values close to zero.

commands.name: CONCAT
commands.description: Joins two lists into one.

commands.name: ΔLIST
commands.description: A list of the differences between neighbouring elements, one element shorter than the list.

examples.comment: The differences 5-3, 8-5 and 12-8

commands.name: MAKELIST
commands.description: Builds a list by evaluating an expression as a variable steps from a start to an end value: MAKELIST(expression,variable,start,end,step).

examples.comment: A^2 for A from 1 to 4 in steps of 1

commands.name: ΠLIST
commands.description: Multiplies all elements of a list.

commands.name: POS
commands.description: Where an element first occurs in a list, or 0 when it is not there.

examples.comment: The 12 is the 3rd element of the list

commands.name: REVERSE
commands.description: The list with its elements in reverse order.

commands.name: SIZE
commands.description: How many elements a list has. For a matrix, its rows and columns as a list.

commands.name: ΣLIST
commands.description: Adds all elements of a list.

commands.name: SORT
commands.description: The list sorted in ascending order.

commands.name: ITERATE
commands.description: Evaluates an expression again and again, each time with the last result as the variable's new value: ITERATE(expression,variable,start,times).

examples.comment: Squares X three times from the start value 2: 4, 16, 256

commands.name: RECURSE
commands.description: Defines a sequence by a recurrence, usually stored into a function such as U1(N): RECURSE(name,term-n,term1,term2).

commands.name: COLNORM
commands.description: The largest sum of absolute values found in any column of a matrix.

examples.comment: Stores a 2 by 2 matrix in M1; its columns sum to 4 and 6 in absolute value

commands.name: COND
commands.description: How sensitive a square matrix is to errors, measured with its column norm.

examples.comment: The column norm 2 times that of the inverse, 1, gives 2

commands.name: CROSS
commands.description: Cross product of two vectors.

examples.comment: M1 and M2 hold the x and y unit vectors; their cross product is the z unit vector

commands.name: DET
commands.description: Determinant of a square matrix.

commands.name: DOT
commands.description: Dot product of two vectors or matrices of the same size.

commands.name: EIGENVAL
commands.description: Eigenvalues of a square matrix, returned as a vector.

examples.comment: The eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix are its diagonal entries

commands.name: EIGENVV
commands.description: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues of a square matrix, returned as a list holding two arrays.

commands.name: IDENMAT
commands.description: A square matrix of the given size with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

commands.name: INVERSE
commands.description: Inverse of a square matrix; complex matrices work too.

commands.name: LQ
commands.description: Splits a matrix into a lower trapezoidal, an orthogonal and a permutation matrix, returned as a list.

commands.name: LSQ
commands.description: Least-squares solution of minimum norm for a system given by two matrices.

commands.name: LU
commands.description: Splits a square matrix into a lower triangular, an upper triangular and a permutation matrix, returned as a list.

commands.name: MAKEMAT
commands.description: Builds a matrix of the given rows and columns from an expression; I and J in it stand for the row and the column: MAKEMAT(expression,rows,columns).

examples.comment: A 2 by 2 matrix whose entry is row I plus column J

commands.name: QR
commands.description: Splits a matrix into an orthogonal, an upper trapezoidal and a permutation matrix, returned as a list.

commands.name: RANK
commands.description: Rank of a matrix.

examples.comment: The second row is twice the first, so the rank is 1

commands.name: ROWNORM
commands.description: The largest sum of absolute values found in any row of a matrix.

examples.comment: Stores a 2 by 2 matrix in M1; its rows sum to 3 and 7 in absolute value

commands.name: RREF
commands.description: The matrix in reduced row echelon form; the last column of an augmented matrix then holds the solution of its linear system.

examples.comment: Stores an augmented matrix in M1; the last column holds the solution x = -1, y = 2

commands.name: SCHUR
commands.description: Splits a square matrix into a list of two matrices, orthogonal (or unitary) and upper triangular.

commands.name: SPECNORM
commands.description: Spectral norm of a matrix.

commands.name: SPECRAD
commands.description: Largest absolute value among a square matrix's eigenvalues (its spectral radius).

commands.name: SVD
commands.description: Splits a matrix into two square orthogonal matrices and a vector of singular values, returned as a list.

commands.name: SVL
commands.description: Singular values of a matrix, returned as a vector.

commands.name: TRACE
commands.description: Sum of the diagonal elements of a square matrix.

commands.name: TRN
commands.description: Swaps the rows and columns of a matrix. A complex matrix is also conjugated.

commands.name: POLYCOEF
commands.description: The coefficients of the polynomial that has the given roots.

examples.comment: The roots 2 and -3 give X^2 + X - 6

commands.name: POLYEVAL
commands.description: Value of a polynomial, given by its coefficients, at a point.

examples.comment: The polynomial X^2 + 2X - 3 at X = 2

commands.name: POLYFORM
commands.description: Rewrites an expression as a polynomial in the given variable.

commands.name: POLYROOT
commands.description: The roots of a polynomial given by its coefficients.

examples.comment: The roots of X^2 + X - 6

commands.name: COMB
commands.description: How many ways there are to pick r of n things when the order does not matter: COMB(n,r).

commands.name: PERM
commands.description: How many ways there are to pick r of n things in order: PERM(n,r).

commands.name: RANDOM
commands.description: A random number between 0 and 1. RANDSEED sets where the sequence starts.

commands.name: UTPC
commands.description: Probability that a chi-squared variable with the given degrees of freedom is larger than the value: UTPC(degrees,value).

commands.name: UTPF
commands.description: Probability that a Snedecor F variable, with the degrees of freedom of its numerator and denominator given, is larger than the value.

commands.name: UTPN
commands.description: Probability that a normal variable with the given mean and variance is larger than the value: UTPN(mean,variance,value).

examples.comment: Mean 0, variance 1, at the value 0: half of the probability lies above

commands.name: UTPT
commands.description: Probability that a Student's t variable with the given degrees of freedom is larger than the value.

commands.name: CEILING
commands.description: The smallest whole number not below the value.

commands.name: DEG→RAD
commands.description: Converts an angle from degrees to radians.

commands.name: FLOOR
commands.description: The largest whole number not above the value.

examples.comment: A negative value rounds down, away from zero

commands.name: FNROOT
commands.description: Searches for a value of the variable that makes the expression zero, starting from a guess: FNROOT(expression,variable,guess).

examples.comment: Finds where X^2-2 is zero, starting the search at X = 1: the square root of 2

commands.name: FRAC
commands.description: The part of the value after the decimal point.

commands.name: HMS→
commands.description: Converts a time or angle written H.MMSS to decimal hours or degrees.

examples.comment: 8.3 is 8h30m, which is 8.5 hours

commands.name: →HMS
commands.description: Converts decimal hours or degrees to the H.MMSS form.

examples.comment: 8.5 hours is 8h30m

commands.name: INT
commands.description: The value with its fractional part dropped.

commands.name: MANT
commands.description: The significant digits of a value, without its power of ten.

commands.name: MAX
commands.description: The larger of two values.

commands.name: MIN
commands.description: The smaller of two values.

commands.name: MOD
commands.description: Remainder of the value before MOD divided by the value after it.
x percent of y: %(x,y) is x times y divided by 100.

commands.name: %CHANGE
commands.description: How many percent y is above (or below) x: %CHANGE(x,y).

examples.comment: From 20 to 50 is a rise of 150 percent

commands.name: %TOTAL
commands.description: What percentage of x the value y is: %TOTAL(x,y).

examples.comment: 50 is 250 percent of 20

commands.name: RAD→DEG
commands.description: Converts an angle from radians to degrees.

commands.name: ROUND
commands.description: Rounds a value to the given number of decimal places; a negative count rounds to that many significant digits.

commands.name: SIGN
commands.description: 1 for a positive value, −1 for a negative one, 0 for zero. For a complex number, the unit vector in its direction.

commands.name: TRUNCATE
commands.description: Cuts a value off after the given number of decimal places.

commands.name: XPON
commands.description: The power of ten of a value.

examples.comment: 123.4 is 1.234 times 10 to the power 2

commands.name: PREDX
commands.description: The x value the current fit of the Statistics aplet gives for a y value.

commands.name: PREDY
commands.description: The y value the current fit of the Statistics aplet gives for an x value.

commands.name: ISOLATE
commands.description: Solves expression=0 for the first occurrence of a variable. Formal names s1 and n1 in the result stand for any sign and any integer.

commands.name: LINEAR?
commands.description: 1 when the expression is linear in the variable, else 0.

commands.name: QUAD
commands.description: Solves a quadratic expression=0 for a variable; the formal name s1 in the result stands for either sign.

examples.comment: Solves X^2 - 4 = 0; s1*4/2 stands for 2 and -2

commands.name: QUOTE
commands.description: Keeps an expression from being evaluated, so that it is stored as written.
Evaluates the expression before it with variables set to the values given after it: expression|(X=3).

examples.comment: Sets X to 3 in the expression 3*(X+1)

commands.description: 1 when the first value is smaller than the second, else 0.
1 when the first value is not larger than the second, else 0.
1 when both values are equal, else 0. This is the test; = builds an equation.
1 when the values differ, else 0.
1 when the first value is larger than the second, else 0.
1 when the first value is not smaller than the second, else 0.

commands.name: IFTE
commands.description: The second argument when the test is non-zero, else the third: IFTE(test,true,false).

examples.comment: The test 1 is non-zero, so the result is the second argument, 5

commands.name: NOT
commands.description: 1 when the value is zero, else 0.

commands.name: OR
commands.description: 1 when either value is non-zero, else 0.

commands.name: XOR
commands.description: 1 when exactly one of the two values is non-zero, else 0.

commands.name: ACOT
commands.description: The angle whose cotangent is the value.

commands.name: ACSC
commands.description: The angle whose cosecant is the value.

commands.name: ASEC
commands.description: The angle whose secant is the value.

commands.name: COT
commands.description: Cosine divided by sine.

examples.comment: The angle mode is radians, so 1 means 1 radian

commands.name: CSC
commands.description: One divided by the sine.

examples.comment: The angle mode is radians, so 1 means 1 radian

commands.name: SEC
commands.description: One divided by the cosine.

commands.name: CHECK
commands.description: Ticks function number n in the current aplet's Symbolic view, so it is plotted and tabulated: CHECK n.

commands.name: SELECT
commands.description: Makes the named aplet the current one: SELECT name. Put a name with spaces in quotes.

commands.name: SETVIEWS
commands.description: Replaces the current aplet's VIEWS menu with entries given as trios of prompt, program name and view number, separated by semicolons.

commands.name: UNCHECK
commands.description: Clears the tick of function number n in the current aplet: UNCHECK n.

commands.name: IF
commands.description: Starts a branch: IF test THEN commands [ELSE commands] END.

commands.name: THEN
commands.description: Starts the commands an IF, IFERR or CASE branch runs when its test holds.

commands.name: ELSE
commands.description: Starts the commands an IF runs when its test fails.

commands.name: END
commands.description: Ends a branch or loop: IF, CASE, IFERR, FOR, DO and WHILE.

commands.name: CASE
commands.description: Runs the first of several IF test THEN commands END clauses whose test holds; the whole ends with END.

commands.name: IFERR
commands.description: Runs the commands after THEN when the commands before it cause an error, instead of stopping the program.

commands.name: RUN
commands.description: Runs a program by its name: RUN name, in quotes when it has spaces.

commands.name: STOP
commands.description: Ends the running program.

commands.name: ARC
commands.description: Draws an arc: ARC x;y;r;from;to draws part of a circle of radius r around (x,y) between two angles.

commands.name: BOX
commands.description: Draws a rectangle from two opposite corners: BOX x1;y1;x2;y2.

commands.name: ERASE
commands.description: Clears the display.

commands.name: FREEZE
commands.description: Keeps what a program drew on the display until any key.

commands.name: LINE
commands.description: Draws a line between two points: LINE x1;y1;x2;y2.

commands.name: PIXOFF
commands.description: Turns off the dot at a point: PIXOFF x;y.

commands.name: PIXON
commands.description: Turns on the dot at a point: PIXON x;y.

commands.name: TLINE
commands.description: Inverts every dot along a line, so drawing the same line twice removes it: TLINE x1;y1;x2;y2.

commands.name: DISPLAY→
commands.description: Saves the display in a graphic variable (G0 to G9): DISPLAY→ name.

commands.name: →DISPLAY
commands.description: Shows a graphic variable on the display: →DISPLAY name.

commands.name: →GROB
commands.description: Draws an expression as a graphic in font size 1, 2 or 3 and stores it: →GROB name;expression;size.

commands.name: GROBNOT
commands.description: Inverts every dot of a graphic variable.

commands.name: GROBOR
commands.description: Lays one graphic over another with logical OR, its top left corner at a position: GROBOR name1;(x,y);name2.

commands.name: GROBXOR
commands.description: Lays one graphic over another with logical XOR, its top left corner at a position: GROBXOR name1;(x,y);name2.

commands.name: MAKEGROB
commands.description: Builds a graphic from a width, a height and hexadecimal data: MAKEGROB name;width;height;hex.

commands.name: PLOT→
commands.description: Saves the Plot view as a graphic: PLOT→ name.

commands.name: →PLOT
commands.description: Puts a graphic into the Plot view: →PLOT name.

commands.name: REPLACE
commands.description: Overwrites part of a graphic, list or matrix with another one, from a start position: REPLACE name;start;object.

commands.name: SUB
commands.description: Copies part of a graphic, list or matrix, from a start to an end position, into a variable: SUB name;object;start;end.

commands.name: ZEROGROB
commands.description: Creates an empty graphic of a width and height: ZEROGROB name;width;height.

commands.name: FOR
commands.description: Counted loop: FOR variable=start TO end [STEP increment]; commands END.

commands.name: TO
commands.description: Gives the end value of a FOR loop.

commands.name: STEP
commands.description: Gives the increment of a FOR loop; without it the step is 1.

commands.name: DO
commands.description: Loop that runs at least once: DO commands UNTIL test END.

commands.name: UNTIL
commands.description: Gives the test that ends a DO loop.

commands.name: WHILE
commands.description: Loop that runs while a test holds: WHILE test REPEAT commands END.

commands.name: REPEAT
commands.description: Starts the commands of a WHILE loop.

commands.name: BREAK
commands.description: Leaves the loop it is in.

commands.name: ADDCOL
commands.description: Inserts a vector as a new column before the given column of a matrix variable: ADDCOL name;vector;column.

commands.name: ADDROW
commands.description: Inserts a vector as a new row before the given row of a matrix variable: ADDROW name;vector;row.

commands.name: DELCOL
commands.description: Removes a column from a matrix variable: DELCOL name;column.

commands.name: DELROW
commands.description: Removes a row from a matrix variable: DELROW name;row.

commands.name: EDITMAT
commands.description: Opens the matrix editor on a matrix variable; a program goes on when OK is pressed.

commands.name: RANDMAT
commands.description: Fills a matrix variable (M0 to M9) with random whole numbers between −9 and 9: RANDMAT M;rows;cols.

commands.name: REDIM
commands.description: Changes the size of a matrix or vector variable; the size is a list {rows,columns} or {n}.

commands.name: SCALE
commands.description: Multiplies one row of a matrix variable by a value: SCALE name;value;row.

commands.name: SCALEADD
commands.description: Adds value times row r1 of a matrix variable to its row r2: SCALEADD M;value;r1;r2.

commands.name: SWAPCOL
commands.description: Exchanges two columns of a matrix variable.

commands.name: SWAPROW
commands.description: Exchanges two rows of a matrix variable.

commands.name: PRDISPLAY
commands.description: Prints the display on an infrared printer.

commands.name: PRHISTORY
commands.description: Prints everything in HOME's history on an infrared printer.

commands.name: PRVAR
commands.description: Prints a variable's name and contents; PRVAR name;PROG or name;NOTE prints a program or a note.

commands.name: BEEP
commands.description: Sounds a tone: BEEP frequency;seconds.

commands.name: CHOOSE
commands.description: Shows a choose box and stores the number of the item picked: CHOOSE variable;title;item1;item2...

commands.name: DISP
commands.description: Shows text and values on a line of the display, 1 at the top to 7 at the bottom: DISP line;items.

commands.name: DISPTIME
commands.description: Shows the date and time.

commands.name: GETKEY
commands.description: Waits for a key and stores its code (row, column and shift plane) in a variable.

commands.name: INPUT
commands.description: Shows an input form with one field and stores what is entered: INPUT variable;title;label;help;default.

commands.name: MSGBOX
commands.description: Shows text and values in a box until OK is pressed.

commands.name: PROMPT
commands.description: Asks for the value of a one-letter variable in a box titled with its name.

commands.name: WAIT
commands.description: Pauses a program for a number of seconds.

commands.name: DO1VSTATS
commands.description: Computes the one-variable statistics of a data set (H1 to H5) into their variables.

commands.name: RANDSEED
commands.description: Sets the starting point of RANDOM's sequence.

commands.name: SETFREQ
commands.description: Sets where a one-variable data set takes its frequencies from: a column or a number.

commands.name: SETSAMPLE
commands.description: Sets the column a one-variable data set takes its values from.

commands.name: DO2VSTATS
commands.description: Computes the two-variable statistics of a data set (S1 to S5) into their variables.

commands.name: SETDEPEND
commands.description: Sets the column of a two-variable data set's dependent values.

commands.name: SETINDEP
commands.description: Sets the column of a two-variable data set's independent values.
